seoTitle: How to Archive a User in Google Workspace (2026)
metaDescription: Learn how to archive a Google Workspace user instead of deleting them, preserving emails and files while reducing your licensing costs.
intro: When an employee leaves or changes roles, archiving their account lets you retain important emails and files without paying for an active license. This guide explains how to convert a user to archived status in Google Workspace and what happens to their data.

steps.heading: Decide if archiving fits your needs
steps.body: Archiving is best when you need to keep a former employee's data for compliance or legal reasons but don't need them to actively use the account.

steps.heading: Convert the user in the Admin Console
steps.body: Locate the user account and select the option to convert it to an archived user rather than suspending or deleting it.

steps.heading: Understand data access changes
steps.body: Once archived, the user loses active access to Gmail, Drive, and Calendar, but their data remains stored securely and searchable by admins.

steps.heading: Review pricing considerations
steps.body: Archived users typically cost less than a full license, though there may still be a reduced archived-user fee depending on your Workspace edition.

steps.heading: Know how to restore an archived user later
steps.body: If needed, you can convert an archived user back to active status, restoring their full access and data in the process.

faq.question: What's the difference between archiving and suspending a user?
faq.answer: Suspending blocks access but still bills at the full license rate, while archiving is designed specifically to reduce costs while preserving data long-term.

faq.question: Can I still search an archived user's emails?
faq.answer: Yes, admins can typically still access and search an archived user's email and file data even though the user themselves can't log in.

faq.question: Does archiving delete the user's Drive files?
faq.answer: No, archiving preserves the user's Drive files along with their Gmail data rather than removing anything.

faq.question: How much does archiving a user cost compared to deleting them?
faq.answer: Archiving usually carries a reduced fee compared to a full active license, making it cheaper than keeping the seat active, though not entirely free like deletion.
